blogs.title: When the Headache is the First Sign: Concurrent Diagnosis of Systemic Behçet's and Acute Neuro-Behçet's
blogs.description: This post explores the classic 'delayed' paradigm of neuro-Behçet's disease versus the rare reality of concurrent presentation. We analyze why acute meningoencephalitis can precede parenchymal MRI findings, the pitfalls of relying on brain imaging in early-stage neuro-inflammation, and how to recognize subtle mucocutaneous clues (oral/genital ulcers) that trigger a shift from infectious workups to rheumatologic diagnosis.

blogs.title: Beyond the Brain: SIADH as a Paraneoplastic-Like Manifestation of CNS Inflammation in Behçet's
blogs.description: While SIADH is often attributed to drugs or malignancy, this case highlights its emergence as a direct consequence of CNS inflammation in acute neuro-Behçet's. We discuss the proposed mechanistic link via IL-6 mediated ADH dysregulation, review the differential diagnosis for hyponatremia in febrile patients with neurological symptoms, and emphasize why recognizing this triad (fever + headache + hyponatremia) is critical before labeling it idiopathic.

blogs.title: Silent Clues: Hiccups and Rhabdomyolysis as Markers of Severe Hyponatremic Encephalopathy
blogs.description: Hyponatremia often presents nonspecifically, but this case underscores two distinct 'red flags': persistent hiccups and elevated creatine kinase indicative of rhabdomyolysis. This educational piece details the pathophysiology linking severe hyponatremia to diaphragmatic spasm and skeletal muscle injury, urging clinicians to include CK levels and ask about hiccups in any patient with suspected CNS inflammation or SIADH.

blogs.title: Steroid-Sparing Success? Re-evaluating Colchicine Monotherapy in Acute Neuro-Behçet's
blogs.description: Standard guidelines recommend aggressive immunosuppression (steroids/cyclophosphamide) for acute neuro-Behçet's, yet this patient responded dramatically to colchicine alone. We critically examine this outlier against current literature, discussing whether colchicine has a role as first-line therapy for mild-to-moderate meningeal-predominant presentations or if this represents a unique window for spontaneous remission. The post weighs risks/benefits of steroid-sparing strategies in complex inflammatory cases.

blogs.title: The Diagnostic Trap: Navigating Fever and Hyponatremia When Infection is Excluded
blogs.description: This post breaks down the stepwise diagnostic reasoning used in this case where standard infectious etiologies (viral, bacterial, TB) were rigorously ruled out despite high fever and CSF pleocytosis. We discuss when to pivot from 'treat until proven guilty' antibiotics/antivirals to considering rare autoimmune entities like Behçet's or Sarcoidosis, emphasizing the value of clinical scoring systems over incidental lab markers like sIL-2R or HLA-B51.
